caption: The drawing depicts a terrestrial globe mounted on a wooden stand. The globe itself is shaded in muted tones of beige, light brown, and gray, with continents outlined and roughly shaded in a rusty brown color, while the oceans are a pale grayish-blue. The globe is held in place by an axis that passes through its poles, supported by four knobs—one on either side of the axis attached to the wooden circular ring. The wooden stand consists of a thick circular ring that encircles the globe's equator and is supported by three outwardly angled, sturdy legs. The wood of the stand is a reddish-brown color, with some gradient suggesting a polished or varnished surface. In the upper left corner, there is a small annexed rectangle containing a schematic line drawing of the object in red ink, showing measurements labeled “B,” “L,” and “H” (presumably for breadth, length, and height). The drawing is centered inside a thin red-bordered rectangular frame and is signed “Edward L. Larsen Dec 156-1” in red ink in the bottom right corner.
title: Globe
